title: Who uses bash?
briefing: /etc/passwd lists every account, one per line, fields split by colons:
The last field is the login shell.
tips: `grep WORD file` keeps matching lines. `cut -d: -f1` keeps the first colon-field.
objective: Write the username of every account whose login shell is /bin/bash (one per line) into ~/bash_users.txt.
hints: First keep only the lines that mention /bin/bash, then keep only the name column.
`grep /bin/bash /etc/passwd` filters the lines; pipe into `cut -d: -f1` for the names.
explanation: `grep` filters lines, `cut -d: -f1` extracts a column, and `|` glues them together. This grep-then-cut pattern pulls structured data out of any colon- or comma-separated file.
